title: Right exactness of completed constant finite modules
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative Noetherian ring, I an ideal and C its I-adic completion. For any C-linear map f:P -> Q between finite C-modules, the functor completion of [def-weil-pbc-completed-constant-completion-functor] preserves the cokernel diagram parallelPair f 0. This assertion concerns the inverse limit of constant quotient modules alone: it does not use a scalar-extension map or a tensor-to-limit comparison.

source.place: Tags 093J--093M, together with More on Algebra Tag 0912

proof.text: For each site object U, let E_U send an A-module to the sections of its constant module sheaf, restricted along the constant coefficient unit. This functor is additive and left exact, by exactness of constant module sheafification and preservation of limits by evaluation and restriction of scalars. A surjective module map has a section as a map of sets. Apply the constant set sheaf functor and constantCommuteCompose to obtain a right inverse on sections. Hence E_U is exact and preserves surjections. This argument works directly on the given pro-etale site, with its original universes.

For a surjection M -> N, every quotient M/I^(n+1)M -> N/I^(n+1)N is surjective, and its kernel is the image of the fixed module ker(M -> N). These facts remain true after E_U. Choose a lift at level zero and proceed recursively: correct any lift at level n+1 by an element of E_U(ker(M -> N)) so that its transition equals the chosen lift at level n. The limit universal property produces a section lifting any section of completion(N). Thus completion preserves sectionwise surjections, without finiteness.

Put C=AdicCompletion I A and J=IC. The ring C is Noetherian. For a C-module V, restriction of scalars identifies J^n V with I^n V, by restrictScalars_map_smul_eq and Ideal.map_pow. Given an injection f:P -> Q with Q finite, apply Artin-Rees to its image in Q. There exists c such that f(x) in I^(n+c+1)Q implies x in I^(n+1)P, uniformly in n. Exactness of E_U transfers this kernel containment to the corresponding maps on constant sections.

For an exact sequence 0 -> P -> Q -> R -> 0 with Q finite and a section y in the kernel of completion(Q) -> completion(R), choose at every level n a preimage z_n in E_U(P) of its quotient section y_n. Let a_n be the image of z_(n+c) in E_U(P/I^(n+1)P). Compatibility of y implies that z_(n+1+c)-z_(n+c) lies in the kernel at level n+c. The uniform Artin-Rees bound therefore makes a_n compatible. It also implies that its image in the quotient of Q is y_n. The limit universal property gives a preimage of y in completion(P), proving sectionwise exactness.

For arbitrary f:P -> Q, factor it as the surjection P -> image(f) followed by the inclusion image(f) -> Q. Apply sectionwise surjectivity to the first map and the preceding exactness result to image(f) -> Q -> Q/image(f). Thus completion(P) -> completion(Q) -> completion(Q/image(f)) is right exact on every object. ModuleCat.isColimitCokernelCofork supplies the sectionwise cokernel universal properties; presheaf evaluation jointly reflects colimits and the sheaf inclusion reflects colimits. Transfer the resulting colimit cocone along isColimitMapCoconeCoforkEquiv to obtain preservation of parallelPair f 0.

proof_origin.place: Artin-Rees (lemma-Artin-Rees, Tag 00IN) and the induced-topology bound (lemma-map-AR), combined with Modules on Sites lemma-constant-exact (Tag 093J). Direct compatible-lift proof, modeled on Mathlib.RingTheory.AdicCompletion.Exactness.map_exact; no tensor-limit comparison.

mathlib_searches.query: For a finite module over a Noetherian adic completion, scalar extension of its constant sheaf to the completed constant ring is the inverse limit of its constant finite quotients
mathlib_searches.results: Ordinary AdicCompletion.ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian and related equivalences; no matching sheaf map or right-exactness result. A second query for constant quotient sheaf cokernels returned AdicCompletion.map_exact, again for ordinary modules.
Five ordinary completion/tensor declarations, with no site or constant-sheaf comparison.

No matching declaration in the Mathlib grep search. Separate project rg inspection found CompletedConstantProjectionMaps and CompletedConstantSheafReduction, which supply the constructions used by the proof.
mathlib_searches.verdict: use existing constructions and ordinary adjunction; isolate two distinct missing steps

mathlib_searches.query: The inverse limit of constant quotient sheaves of finite modules over a Noetherian completed ring preserves cokernels, and the completed constant comparison is an isomorphism for the rank one free module
mathlib_searches.results: Eight results: generic cokernel preservation and module/sheaf limits, ordinary AdicCompletion, and ModuleCat.cokernelIsoRangeQuotient. None establishes the constant quotient sheaf comparison or its right exactness.

from.place: Right exactness of completed constant finite modules

lean.statement:
theorem completion_preservesCokernel (X : Scheme.{u})
    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    {P Q : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (AdicCompletion I A)}
    [Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I A) P] [Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I A) Q]
    (f : P ⟶ Q) :
    PreservesColimit (parallelPair f 0) (completion X I)
